title: CHAPTER XXV. Matthew Insists on Puffed Sleeves
chineseTitle: 第 25 章：马修坚持要泡泡袖

paragraphs.en: Matthew found himself in an awkward situation as he entered the kitchen on a cold December evening. Unaware that Anne and her classmates were rehearsing "The Fairy Queen" in the sitting room, he sat quietly in the woodbox corner, removing his boots. The girls, laughing and chatting, passed through the hall into the kitchen without noticing him.
paragraphs.zh: 马修在寒冷的十二月傍晚踏入厨房时，发现自己陷入了尴尬的局面。他全然不知安妮和她的同学们正在客厅里排练《仙后》，便默默地坐在木箱角上脱下靴子。女孩们说说笑笑地从大厅经过，径直走进了厨房，丝毫没有注意到他的存在。

paragraphs.en: Matthew, feeling shy, retreated to the shadows.
paragraphs.zh: 马修感到有些不好意思，便退到了阴影中。

paragraphs.en: Anne stood among them, lively and animated. But something about her struck Matthew as unusual—something that shouldn't be there. He noticed Anne's brighter face, larger eyes, and more delicate features.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮站在他们中间，显得格外活泼生动。但马修觉得她有些不同寻常——不该有的不同。他注意到安妮的脸色更加红润，眼睛也更大了，五官似乎变得更加精致细腻。

paragraphs.en: Yet, what troubled him most was a difference he couldn’t pinpoint.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，让他最为烦恼的是一个他无法明确指出的差异。

paragraphs.en: Later, after the girls had left for their walk down the frozen lane, Matthew remained puzzled. He didn't want to discuss it with Marilla, who would likely dismiss his concerns. Instead, he turned to his pipe that evening, trying to figure out the issue.
paragraphs.zh: 后来，当女孩们离开去冻车道散步后，马修依然感到困惑。他不想与玛丽拉讨论这个问题，因为她可能会轻视他的担忧。于是那天晚上，他转而抽起了烟斗，试图弄清楚其中的原委。

paragraphs.en: After two hours of contemplation and smoking, Matthew realized Anne was not dressed like her classmates.
paragraphs.zh: 经过两个小时的沉思和抽烟，马修意识到安妮穿的衣服不像她的同学。

paragraphs.en: Matthew became convinced Anne was never dressed like other girls since coming to Green Gables. Marilla clothed her in plain, dark dresses, all similar in pattern. Matthew knew little about fashion but noticed Anne’s sleeves differed from others.
paragraphs.zh: 马修认定自从安妮来到绿山墙农舍后，她从未像其他女孩那样打扮过。玛丽拉给她穿的都是朴素的深色连衣裙，款式都差不多。马修对时尚了解不多，但注意到安妮的袖子与其他人的不同。

paragraphs.en: He decided a single pretty dress for Christmas would be harmless. Matthew bought the dress at Samuel Lawson's store, avoiding William Blair's due to his daughters' presence. He feared their explanations and consultations might overwhelm him.
paragraphs.zh: 他决定给安妮买一件漂亮的圣诞裙子应该无妨。马修在萨缪尔·劳森的商店里买了这件裙子，避开了威廉·布雷尔的店铺，因为布雷尔家的女儿们在那儿。他担心她们的解释和商量可能会让他难以招架。

paragraphs.en: Matthew visited Miss Harris's shop, bewildered by the presence of a new lady clerk named Lucilla. She was flamboyant with a large, drooping hairstyle and an extensive smile that glittered with bangle bracelets.
paragraphs.zh: 马修造访哈里斯小姐的店铺时，对新来的女店员卢西拉感到困惑不已。她打扮得十分夸张，留着一头大而下垂的发型，脸上挂着一抹灿烂的笑容，笑起来连手上的镯子都闪烁生辉。

paragraphs.en: "Can I help you this evening, Mr. Cuthbert?" asked Lucilla briskly as Matthew stammered about needing garden rakes in December.
paragraphs.zh: “卡瑟伯特先生，您今天晚上需要帮忙吗？”卢西拉利索地问道，而马修支支吾吾地说自己十二月里还需要园艺耙子。

paragraphs.en: "I—well, do you have any garden rakes?" Matthew managed to ask.
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，你有园艺耙子吗？”马修挤出话来问。

paragraphs.en: Lucilla was surprised but said they had a few upstairs. When she returned with the rake, Matthew suggested buying hayseed instead. Lucilla explained they only kept it in spring and had none now.
paragraphs.zh: 露西拉有些惊讶，但还是说他们楼上还有一些。当她拿着耙子回来时，马修建议买些草籽。露西拉解释说他们只在春天储备一些，现在没有了。

paragraphs.en: Feeling embarrassed, Matthew took the rake home without paying. He then asked for brown sugar, which Lucilla showed him from a barrel. Matthew bought twenty pounds of it, sweating profusely.
paragraphs.zh: 感到有些尴尬，马修没有付钱就拿走了耙子。随后他请求拿一些红糖，雷切尔从一个木桶里拿出了一些给他。马修买了二十磅红糖，额头渗出了汗珠。

paragraphs.en: By the time he reached home, Matthew was relieved but realized his foolishness. He hid the rake in the tool house and brought the sugar inside to Marilla.
paragraphs.zh: 等他回到家时，马修松了口气，但也意识到自己的愚蠢。他把耙子藏在工具房里，然后把糖带进了屋交给玛丽拉。

paragraphs.en: Matthew decided he needed a woman's help with his project. Marilla was out of the question; she would likely discourage him. He turned to Mrs. Lynde, who readily agreed to pick out a dress for Anne and promised to handle it on her trip to Carmody.
paragraphs.zh: 马修决定他需要一个女人的帮助来完成这个项目。玛丽拉是不行的，她可能会泼冷水。于是他转向了雷切尔·林德太太，后者欣然同意为安妮挑一件衣服，并承诺在去卡姆多伊的旅途中顺便处理这件事。

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Lynde suggested a rich brown color and mentioned William Blair had some new fabric that might be suitable. Matthew asked if she could make the sleeves in the latest style, puffed ones. Mrs. Lynde assured him there was no trouble and would do as he requested.
paragraphs.zh: 雷切尔·林德建议用一种浓棕色，并提到威廉·布莱尔有一些新面料可能合适。马修问她能否把袖子做成最新的样式，也就是蓬松的款式。雷切尔·林德向他保证没问题，会按照他的要求去做。

paragraphs.en: After Matthew left, Mrs. Lynde thought to herself: "Matthew's got his work cut out for him with Anne."
paragraphs.zh: 马修离开后，雷切尔·林德太太心里想着：“马修可得好好费一番心思对付安妮了。”

paragraphs.en: Matthew had something on his mind for two weeks, but Marilla could not guess what it was until Christmas Eve when Mrs. Lynde mentioned the new dress. Marilla behaved well, though she likely distrusted Mrs. Lynde's explanation that Matthew made the dress to avoid Anne finding out too soon.
paragraphs.zh: 马修心中藏着一件事已有两周之久，但直到圣诞节前夕雷切尔·林德提到新裙子时，玛丽拉才猜到了他的心思。尽管玛丽拉表现得井然有序，她其实对林德太太解释说马修做这件裙子是为了避免安妮过早得知这件事持怀疑态度。

paragraphs.en: "Is this what Matthew has been so secretive about for two weeks?" Marilla said stiffly but tolerantly. "I knew he was up to something foolish.
paragraphs.zh: “这就是马修这两周来一直保密的事情吗？”玛丽拉绷着脸，语气却带着几分忍耐地说，“我知道他肯定在搞什么鬼名堂。”

paragraphs.en: I don't think Anne needs more dresses; I made her three good, warm ones this fall. More is sheer extravagance. Those sleeves alone could make a waist.
paragraphs.zh: 我认为安妮不需要更多的裙子了；这个秋天我给她做了三件既实用又保暖的。再多就纯粹是奢侈浪费了。单单那些蓬松的袖子就能做一件衬衫呢。

paragraphs.en: You'll just pamper Anne's vanity, Matthew, and she’s as vain as a peacock now."
paragraphs.zh: 你这样只会纵容安妮的虚荣心，马修，她现在已经骄傲得像只孔雀了。

paragraphs.en: Marilla hoped Anne would be satisfied at last, knowing the girl had been longing for those puffed sleeves since they became popular. "The puffs have grown bigger and more ridiculous; they’re as big as balloons now," Marilla said. "Next year, anyone wearing them will have to go through a door sideways."
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉希望安妮这次终于会满意了，因为她知道那段时间安妮一直渴望拥有这种蓬松袖子。自从蓬松袖子流行起来后，玛丽拉说道：“这些蓬松的袖子越来越大，越来越可笑；现在它们简直像气球一样大。”她接着说，“明年如果还有人穿这样的衣服，恐怕只能侧着身子才能进门了。”

paragraphs.en: Christmas morning dawned on Avonlea, transformed by a light dusting of snow. Anne gazed out her frosted window with delight, marveling at the feathery fir trees and pearl-like birches. The plowed fields were dotted with snowy dimples, and the air was crisp and invigorating.
paragraphs.zh: 圣诞节的晨光洒在埃文利镇上，轻盈的雪花为小镇披上了银装。安妮欣喜地凝望着霜花点缀的窗户，赞叹着那些如羽毛般轻柔的松树和珍珠般的白桦树。犁过的田地上散落着雪点，空气中清新而提神。

paragraphs.en: Anne rushed downstairs, singing until her voice echoed through Green Gables. "Merry Christmas, Marilla! Merry Christmas, Matthew!
paragraphs.zh: 安妮飞快地下楼，边走边唱，歌声在绿山墙农庄回荡。“圣诞快乐，玛丽拉！圣诞快乐，马修！”

paragraphs.en: Isn't it a lovely white Christmas? I'm so glad it's snow-covered. Any other kind doesn’t feel real, does it?"
paragraphs.zh: 不是一场雪白的圣诞多么美妙？我真高兴外面都是雪。其他任何形式的雪都不觉得那么真实，对吧？

paragraphs.en: Matthew sheepishly presented Anne with a wrapped dress, his gaze apologetic as he handed it to her. Marilla pretended to fill the teapot but secretly watched the exchange with interest.
paragraphs.zh: 马修羞涩地把一件包裹好的裙子递给了安妮，眼神中带着歉意。玛丽拉假装在给茶壶加水，实际上却饶有兴致地观察着两人之间的互动。

paragraphs.en: Anne examined the dress reverently. It was beautiful—a soft brown silk with delicate frills and intricate tucks, and a ruffle of lace at the neck. But the sleeves were the highlight: long elbow cuffs with two puffy sections adorned with shirring and brown ribbon bows.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮庄重地审视着这件裙子。它非常美丽，是一件柔软的棕色丝绸制成的连衣裙，上面装饰着精致的花边和复杂的褶皱，在领口处还有一圈蕾丝点缀。但最引人注目的还是那两条袖子：长长的肘部袖口，分成两部分膨胀起来，并且装饰着收腰设计和棕色丝带蝴蝶结。

paragraphs.en: "Matthew," Anne whispered, "this is perfect. I can never thank you enough. Look at those sleeves!
paragraphs.zh: 马修，安妮轻声说道：“这真是太完美了。我永远无法足够感谢你。你看这些袖子！”

paragraphs.en: It feels like a dream."
paragraphs.zh: 这感觉像是一场梦。

paragraphs.en: Marilla interrupted, saying, "Let's have breakfast now. Since Matthew got it for you, make sure to take good care of it. There’s a brown hair ribbon from Mrs. Lynde that matches the dress.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉插话说：“我们现在吃早餐吧。既然马修给你买了这件衣服，可得好好珍惜。那条棕色的发带和裙子很配，是雷切尔·林德太太送的。”

paragraphs.en: Come sit down."
paragraphs.zh: 请坐。

paragraphs.en: Anne was thrilled about her breakfast, finding it unimportant compared to admiring a fashionable dress with puffed sleeves. She felt grateful for Mrs. Lynde's gift and resolved to be a good girl. Diana arrived, wearing a crimson ulster, bringing an unexpected present: a box from Aunt Josephine containing delicate kid slippers.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮对早餐感到非常兴奋，相比之下，她更在意那件时尚的蓬袖连衣裙。她感激雷切尔·林德太太的赠礼，并暗暗下定决心要做一个好女孩。戴安娜这时 arrived，穿着一件朱红色的大衣，还带来了一个意想不到的礼物：一盒来自乔赛亚姑妈的精致羊皮拖鞋。

paragraphs.en: "Look at these," Anne exclaimed, holding the slippers. "They're too beautiful."
paragraphs.zh: “看看这些，”安妮脱口而出，拿着那双拖鞋，“真是太漂亮了。”

paragraphs.en: Diana added that it was providential, as Anne wouldn't have to borrow Ruby's oversized ones anymore. The excitement in Avonlea grew as scholars prepared for the Christmas concert. The evening arrived, and the hall was packed with eager spectators.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜补充说，这真是天赐良机，因为安妮再也不用借鲁比那不合身的袖子了。随着埃文利镇为圣诞音乐会做准备，兴奋之情日益高涨。终于到了晚上，会场里挤满了急切的观众。

paragraphs.en: The concert was a success, with all performers doing well, but Anne shone brightest, even Josie Pye admitted.
paragraphs.zh: 音乐会取得了成功，所有表演者都表现不错，但安妮的光芒最为耀眼，就连乔西·派伊也承认了这一点。

paragraphs.en: Anne sighed contentedly with Diana on their walk home under a starry sky. "Oh, hasn't it been a brilliant evening?" she asked.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮和戴安娜在星光下走回家，满意地叹了口气。“哦，今晚多美好啊？”她问道。

paragraphs.en: Diana replied practically, "Everything went off very well. We made about ten dollars, and Mr. Allan will send an account to the Charlottown papers."
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜实话实说：“一切都进行得很顺利。我们赚了大约十美元，艾伦先生会把账单寄给夏洛特镇的报社。”

paragraphs.en: Anne's recitation had brought down the house, Diana noted. Anne felt proud when her sad recitation was encored. She thought of her puffed sleeves as she stepped onto the platform.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜注意到，安妮的朗诵赢得了满堂喝彩。当她的悲伤朗诵得到了加演时，安妮感到十分自豪。她迈上讲台的时候，不禁想起了自己那蓬松的袖子。

paragraphs.en: Diana remembered how nervous Anne was but praised her performance. "You groaned lovely," Diana assured her.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜记得安妮当时很紧张，但还是称赞了她的表现：“你呻吟得真动人。”她向安妮保证。

paragraphs.en: After the concert, Mrs. Sloane wiped away tears, and Anne felt she had touched someone's heart. The boys' dialogue was fine too; Gilbert Blythe was splendid.
paragraphs.zh: 音乐会结束后，斯洛恩太太擦去了眼泪，安妮觉得自己的表演触动了某人的心弦。男孩子们的对话也很精彩；吉尔伯特·布雷思的表现尤为出色。

paragraphs.en: That night, Marilla and Matthew, who had attended their first concert in twenty years, sat by the kitchen fire. "Well now, I guess our Anne did as well as any of them," said Matthew proudly.
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，玛丽拉和马修坐在厨房的火炉旁，他们已经有二十年没有去听过音乐会了。“我想我们的安妮表现得跟其他人一样出色，”马修自豪地说。

paragraphs.en: Marilla admitted Anne was bright and looked nice at the concert. She had been against the scheme but saw no real harm in it. Proud of Anne, Marilla didn't tell her so.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉承认安妮确实聪明，她在音乐会上的样子也很不错。她原本反对这个计划，但觉得这也没什么大不了的坏处。尽管为安妮感到骄傲，玛丽拉却没有直接说出来。

paragraphs.en: Matthew told Anne he was proud of her before she went upstairs. They needed to find ways to help Anne in the future since Avonlea school wouldn’t be enough by then.
paragraphs.zh: 马修在安妮上楼前告诉她，他为她感到骄傲。他们需要找到方法在未来帮助安妮，因为到了那时埃文利学校的教育已经不够了。

paragraphs.en: Marilla noted Anne would turn thirteen in March and seemed a big girl now. Mrs. Lynde's dress made Anne look taller. Marilla thought sending Anne to Queen’s after some time might be best, but it was too early to discuss that.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉注意到安妮三月份就要十三岁了，看起来已经是个大姑娘了。雷切尔·林德太太的衣服穿在安妮身上让她显得更高挑了一些。玛丽拉觉得过段时间把安妮送到女王学院去或许是最好的选择，但眼下还为时尚早，不宜讨论此事。

paragraphs.en: Matthew suggested it was good to think about such matters often.
paragraphs.zh: 马修建议经常思考这类事情是有好处的。
